tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Search the public Krate gallery for apps by words. Results are ranked by how well the words match the app's name, then its description and publisher. Each result has the app's link (opens in Krate), a link that opens it in a browser tab, what it is allowed to do in plain words, its size, and whether

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: One public Krate app's details, from its link or id: what it does, what it is allowed to do in plain words, its versions, size, publisher and signature, its link and its browser link. Accepts a hub link (https://hub.krate.tech/a/..., /run/...), the app's own id (v followed by 11 hex characters), a s

tools.name: list_featured
tools.description: The Krate gallery's front shelves: the apps picked to start with, and the newest apps, each with its link, what it is allowed to do in plain words, its size and its publisher.

tools.name: get_krate_guide
tools.description: Krate's reference for writing a Krate app (a native app for Windows, macOS and Linux that also opens in a browser): the files an app is made of (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, manifest.toml), the API it may use, the permissions it may declare, the mistakes that fail a first build, and worked examples. No s

tools.name: search
tools.description: Searches Krate's public apps and Krate's guide to making an app. Each result has an id, a title and a link; the guide's id is krate-guide.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: One Krate app or Krate's guide in full, by the id a result carries: an app's details and permissions in plain words, or the whole guide to making an app.

tools.name: build_app
tools.description: Builds a real app the person keeps: one small file that runs natively on Windows, macOS and Linux and opens from a link in any browser, phones included. A Krate app keeps its own data on the device and works offline; with the person's permission it can print to a printer they pick with no print dial

tools.name: build_status
tools.description: The state of a Krate build, by its build id: still building, failed, or published. A failed build's answer has Krate's check in its own words: the stage, what went wrong and how to fix it. A published build's answer has the app's link and a browser link that opens it on any device, nothing to instal

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
